key_insight: OphthaDT is an LLM-based digital twin that turns longitudinal ophthalmology records into structured narratives to forecast future visual acuity, especially in complex, variable disease courses.
clinical_relevance: This could improve trial analysis and precision medicine in ophthalmology by enabling better BCVA trajectory prediction from irregular real-world follow-up data.
method: Serialized multimodal patient histories into structured text narratives
Trained and evaluated on 3,220 patients from four Phase III trials
Forecasted best corrected visual acuity up to 100 weeks without imputation
evidence_signal: Across benchmarks, OphthaDT showed the lowest error in nAMD with a 6.0% average MAE reduction versus all baselines, and was competitive in DME while outperforming Random Forest and XGBoost by 2.6% and 6.9% MAE on average.
watch_item: Results come from clinical trial data, so performance and generalizability in broader real-world ophthalmology settings still need validation.
paper_title: OphthaDT: Generative Digital Twins for Forecasting Visual Acuity Trajectories in Ophthalmology
